rounds.text: Shanti Gold International Ltd is substantially under-appreciated by the market, trading at a P/E of just 11.69x against a sector benchmark of 26.71x [E5] and an EV/EBITDA of 8.82x versus the sector's 14.61x [E10]. This attractive valuation is paired with exceptional operational efficiency, boasting an ROE of 23.42% and ROCE of 24.85%, which massively outperform their respective sector benchmarks of 8.17% and 10.06% [E8, E9]. The company's fundamental strength is further validated by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 415 per share, offering a 24.9% margin of safety over the current market price [E18, E19]. Growth catalysts are robust, with management sticking to strong guidance of 50% to 60% value growth and 30% to 40% volume growth for the year [E44], underpinned by the recent commencement of the Marol facility and the upcoming Jaipur plant [E50, E51]. Institutional conviction is clearly strengthening, evidenced by a positive institutional money flow and a rising foreign institutional holding of 4.63% [E15, E17]. Conceded: promoter holding decreased by 4.54 percentage points over the period and the company experienced negative cash flows from maintaining ready jewellery stock [E14, E62].

Conceded: [E18], [E19], [E20], [E21], [E22], [E23], [E24], [E25]. Despite a strong near-term technical and valuation backdrop, Shanti Gold International Ltd carries fundamental operational and structural risks that warrant caution. Most notably, the company experienced negative cash flows directly resulting from its business model of maintaining ready jewellery stock rather than operating on an order-to-order basis [E62]. To fund this aggressive growth strategy and fuel its working capital needs, the company approved a rights issue to raise up to INR 100 crores, which will be invested completely in gold and working capital [E59, E61]. Furthermore, promoter holding has declined from 74.89% in September 2025 to 70.35% as of August 2026, alongside a sharp drop in domestic institutional holdings from 4.01% to 1.80% [E14, E16]. Compounding these insider and structural pressures, the company previously exited Gold Metal Loans specifically because of high volatility in gold prices [E63]. Finally, reported margins in the latest period benefited from an artificial, unrealized inventory gain of roughly 2% to 2.5% caused by a change in inventory accounting from FIFO to the weighted average cost method [E54].

Conceded: [E62]. While the bear highlights negative cash flows from maintaining ready stock, this operational model directly powers the company's aggressive and material top-line expansion, enabling massive demand capture in both local and export markets [E48, E58]. Conceded: [E54]. Although inventory accounting shifted from FIFO to WAC, the resulting 2% to 2.5% unrealized gain merely coincides with a broader structural growth story backed by robust return metrics, including an ROE of 23.42% and ROCE of 24.85% that heavily outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E9]. Conceded: [E14, E16]. While promoter and domestic institutional holdings saw adjustments, foreign institutional investors increased their stake by 1.95 percentage points to 4.63%, driving a net positive institutional money flow of +2.93 percentage points [E15, E17]. Furthermore, the bear's concern over funding is precisely addressed by the INR 100 crores rights issue meant to fuel ongoing capacity expansion, including the Marol facility and the upcoming Jaipur plant [E50, E51, E59]. Finally, exiting Gold Metal Loans was a prudent risk-management maneuver away from high gold price volatility, allowing the firm to navigate elevated gold prices while keeping demand trends resilient [E49, E63].

Conceded: [E48]. The bull argues that maintaining ready stock powers aggressive top-line expansion, yet management explicitly admits this business model directly causes negative cash flows [E58, E62]. While the bull dismisses the 2% to 2.5% FIFO-to-WAC inventory shift as a minor coincidence, this accounting change artificially inflated Q1 results with unrealized gains that distort true operational profitability [E54]. Regarding institutional support, the bull highlights foreign inflows [E15, E17], but ignores the troubling reality that domestic institutions dumped their holdings, dropping from 4.01% to 1.80%, alongside a notable promoter sell-off of 4.54 percentage points [E14, E16, E31]. The bull portrays the exit from Gold Metal Loans as a prudent risk-management move [E63], but abandoning these loans due to high gold price volatility underscores the extreme vulnerability the company faces in managing raw material cost swings. Finally, while the bull leans on forward-looking growth targets [E44, E45], management itself explicitly warns that all these forward-looking statements are subject to known and unknown risks and uncertainties that remain difficult to predict [E64].
